1.Introduction Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in the world and the fourth most common cause of cancer -related mortality 1–3. However, if detected and treated at an early stage, a favorable prognosis is expected. Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) is widely used in the prevention of colorectal cancer. It is performed by injecting normal saline into the submucosal layer between the lesion and the muscle layer to protrude the mucosa and then entrappe d with a snare and resection using electrocautery 4. However, some proficiency in the method of injection and snaring is required, and The en bloc resection rate decreases when the polyp size exceeds 10 mm. The resulting high local recurrence rate after piecemeal resection is clinically problematic 5,6. Recently, underwater EMR (UEMR) has emerged by Bimmoeller et al. 7 as an alternative to conventional EMR (CEMR) and is reported to be effective for removing flat or large colorectal polyps. With UEMR, the bo wel lumen is filled with water instead of air, and the lesion is captured and resected with a snare without submucosal injection of normal saline. Compared to CEMR, it is easier to snare large colorectal polyps, residual recurrent lesions, and depressed le sions, and has the potential to improve treatment outcomes. RCTs compared to CEMR have shown significantly higher R0 resection rates for UEMR 8 and significantly shorter procedure time than CEMR 9. Although a meta -analysis of UEMR has shown efficacy and sa fety, the superiority of UEMR over CEMR has not been sufficiently examined because it was not compared with CEMR 10 or because it was compared with CEMR in a mixture of cohort studies and RCTs 11. Therefore, we exclude cohort studies and conduct a meta-analysis with additional RCTs. 2.Research question The effectiveness of UEMR compared with CEMR for endoscopic removal of sessile colorectal lesions. P: Colorectal lesion I: UEMR C: CEMR O: R0 resection 3.Method 3.1 Protocol We used a systematic review protocol template 12. We followed the Preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 for preparing this protocol 13. We will publish this protocol in protocols.io (https://www.protocols.io/). 3.2 Inclusion criteria of the articles for the review 3.2.1 Type of studies We will include randomized controlled trials that assess the effectiveness of UEMR compared with CEMR for endoscopic removal of colorectal lesions. We will not apply language or country restrictions. We will include all papers including published, unpublished articles, abstract of conference and letter. We will exclude duplicate publication, cluster randomized trial, cross-over study, quasi-experimental design, case report and non -human studies. We will not exclude studies based on the observation period or publication year. 3.2.2 Study participants All patients who underwent UEMR or CEMR for colorectal lesions. Inclusion criteria: Adult patients (> 18 years of age) with colorectal lesion Exclusion criteria:

1) Residual and recurrent lesions after endoscopic resection 2) Patients with colitis ulcer, Crohn disease, familial adenomatous polyposis. 3.2.3 Intervention Underwater EMR: complete deflation of the colorectal lumen air and total immersion of the lesion in normal saline. Then snaring the lesion and the surrounding mucosa and resection using electrocautery. 3.2.4 Control CEMR: needle injection of normal saline into the su bmucosa and then entrapment of the mucosal protrusion with a snare and resection using electrocautery. 3.3 Type of outcomes 3.3.1 Primary outcomes 1. Proportion of R0 resection Definition: proportion of R0 resection is calculated as the number of R0 rese ction divided by the total number of lesions. R0 resection was defined as en bloc resection with a histologically confirmed negative resection margin. En bloc resection was defined as endoscopically assessed removal of the lesion in one piece. Period: 2. Mean procedure time Definition: The procedure time in the UEMR group was measured from the start of immersion in normal saline from the endoscope until complete removal of the polyp. The procedure time in the CEMR group was measured from insertion of t he injection needle until complete removal of the polyp. Period: 3.3.2 Secondary outcomes 1. Proportion of en block resection Definition: proportion of en block resection is calculated as the number of en block resection divided by the total number of lesions. En bloc resection was defined as endoscopically assessed removal of the lesion in one piece. Period: 2. All adverse events Definition: Definition of adverse events is set by original authors. Period: during follow up period 3.4 Search method 3.4.1 Electronic search We will search the following databases: 1. the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL); 2. MEDLINE via PubMed; 3. EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog; See Appendix 1, 2, and 3 for the search strategies. 3.4.2 Other resources

We will also search the following databases for ongoing or unpublished trials: 1. the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP); 2. ClinicalTrials.gov; See Appendix 4, 5 for the search strategies. We will check the reference lists of studies, including international guidelines (published by the Japanese Society for Cancer of the Colon and Rectum (JSCCR), the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy and the U.S. Multi -society Task Force on Colo rectal Cancer) 14–16 as well as the reference lists of eligible studies and articles citing eligible studies. We will ask the authors of original studies for unpublished or additional data. 3.5 Data collection and analysis 3.5.1 Selection of the studies Two independent reviewers (TY and NH) will screen titles and abstracts, followed by the assessment of the eligibility based on the full texts. We will contact original authors if relevant data is missing. Disagreements between the two reviewers will be reso lved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter (TS). 3.5.2 Data extraction and management Two reviewers (TY and NH) will perform independent data extraction of the included studies using standardized data collection form. W e will use a pre -checked form using 10 randomly selected studies. The form will include the information on study design, study population, patient characteristics (sex, mean age and number of patients with UEMR and CEMR, number of lesions, mean lesion si ze, lesion location, lesion histological type), R0 resection rate with UEMR and CEMR, en bloc resection rate with UEMR and CEMR, mean procedure time with UEMR and CEMR, and adverse event rate (bleeding and perforation) . Any disagreements will be resolved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter (TS). 3.6 Assessment of risk of bias in included studies Two reviewers (TY and NH) will evaluate the risk of bias independently using the Risk of Bias 2 17. Disagreements between the two reviewers will be discussed, and if this fails, a third reviewer (TS) will be acting as an arbiter, if necessary. 3.7 Measures of treatment effects We will pool the relative risk ratios and the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the following binary variables: R0 resection, en block resection. We will pool the mean differences and the 95% CIs for the following continuous variables: procedure time of UEMR and CEMR If several different scales have been used in the included studies, we will pool the eff ect estimates using standard mean differences (SMDs) 3.8 Unit of analysis issues For continuous data, only the sample size will be reduced; means and standard deviation will remain unchanged.17 Randomised cross-over studies We will consider only data from the first period. Multiple comparisons All intervention groups that are relevant to this review will be included. 3.9 Handling of missing data We will ask not-presented data to the original authors. 3.9.1 Missing outcomes

We will perform the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for all dichotomous data as much as possible. For continuous data, we will not impute missing data based on the recommendation by Cochrane handbook 18. We will perform meta-analysis about the available data in the original study. 3.9.2 Missing statistics When original studies only report standard error or p -value, we will calculate the standard deviation based on the method by Altman 19. If we don't know these values when we contact the authors, standard deviation will be calculated by confidence interval and t -value based on the method by Cochrane handbook 18, or validated method 19. Validity of these methods will be analyzed by sensitivity analysis. 3.10 Assessment of heterogeneity We will evaluate the statistical heterogeneity by visual inspection of the forest plots and calculating the I2 statistic (I2 values of 0% to 40%: might not be important; 30%to 60%: may represent moderate heterogeneity; 50% to 90%: may represent substantial heterogeneity; 75% to 100%: considerable heterogeneity). When there is substantial heterogeneity (I2> 50%), we will assess the reason for the heterogeneity. Cochrane Chi2test (Q -test) will be performed for I2 statistic, and P value less than 0.10 will be defined as statistically significant. 3.11 Assessment of reporting bias We will search the clinical trial registry system (ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP) and will perform extensive literature search for unpublished trials. We will assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot. Egger test will be performed as well. We will not conduct the test when we find less than 10 trials or trials which have similar sample size. We will assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot 3.12 Meta-analysis Meta-analysis will be performed using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4). We will use a random-effects model. 3.13 Subgroup analysis To elucidate the influence of effect modifiers on results, we will evaluate the subgroup anal yses of the primary outcomes on the following factors when sufficient data are available. 1. (For participants) (lesion size ≦20mm vs. > 20mm) 3.14 Sensitivity analysis We will undertake the following sensitivity analyses for the primary outcomes to asse ss whether the results of the review are robust to the decisions made during the review process. 1. Exclusion of studies using imputed statistics. 2. Missing participants: verify the robustness of the results by seeking informative missingness odds ratios 20. 3. Only the participants who complete the study with complete data 4. Summary of findings table Summary of findings table will be made for the following outcome based on the Cochrane handbook18. We will include grading to evaluate the quality of evidence based on the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach for each Summary of findings table 21. 1. Proportion of R0 resection 2. Mean procedure time 3. Proportion of en bloc resection 4. All adverse events
